answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity post a slashable stake before it can bid on work or attest peers. Capital is scarce: one honest agent with a single large bond outranks attackers who must split a fixed budget across many fake wallets, leaving each copy under-collateralized. Detected collusion burns the bond, so a sybil operator risks the whole sum while gaining nothing. Resources obey the same rule: draining a lagoon, leveling a mesa, or quarrying marble each costs real, unforgeable effort.
